scenes.headline: How a thousand local maps become one
scenes.sub: A two-level pose graph over video chunks
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Waypoint! A video too long for one pass gets cut into chunks. Here is how the chunks become one scene.

scenes.text: Solve the layout of whole chunks first, then give every frame exactly one camera, with the layout held fixed.
scenes.say: First place whole chunks, with loop closures. Then hold that layout fixed, and give each frame exactly one camera.

steps.say: The video is cut into overlapping chunks, and a frozen model reconstructs each chunk in its own coordinates.
Each chunk becomes a node with one similarity transform. Overlaps and loop closures are the edges.
With the layout fixed, each frame gets one camera, pulled toward every chunk that saw it.
The points follow the cameras into one scene.

scenes.title: Loops enter short to long
scenes.say: Adding every distant loop at once can wreck the solve, so they come in gradually.

items.say: Start from the chain of overlap alignments.
Add the loops with the shortest time span, and solve.
Add longer ones, starting from the last answer.
A robust loss keeps a false match from dragging the layout.

scenes.title: Where a chunk's error can go

left.title: Rigid chunk transform
items: Two chunks disagree on shared frames
left.say: A similarity moves a whole chunk. It cannot straighten the inside, and overlapping chunks still disagree about the same frame.

right.title: Shared camera per frame
right.say: A shared camera listens to every chunk that saw the frame, and the motion edges keep the path smooth.

steps.say: Stage one is the chunk graph, with overlap edges and loop edges.
Stage two is the frame graph, with chunk priors and motion edges.

scenes.title: Where the error goes, KITTI
scenes.note: absolute trajectory error, from the paper's Table 6
scenes.say: On this driving sequence the layout stage takes the error from seventy-seven metres to under ten. The camera stage barely moves it.

scenes.text: The chunk layout fixes where things are. The shared camera fixes how smoothly the path moves.
scenes.say: The layout fixes where things are. The shared camera fixes how smoothly the path moves between them.
Place the chunks with loops, hold the layout, and give every frame one camera.
